title: Case split on step_async proves composed_invariant inductive
intent: Show that the composed state/network/network invariant `composed_invariant` is an inductive invariant of `step_async` by splitting on the `step_async` constructor, so each of the six resulting cases closes from one `Decomposition` class field or one of five same-file list lemmas, with no per-case mathematics left.

children.name: post_net_analyze_sent_packet
children.statement:
forall h p ms xs ys,
  In p (map (fun m => mkPacket h (fst m) (snd m)) ms ++ xs ++ ys) ->
  (In (pDst p, pBody p) ms /\ h = pSrc p) \/ In p (xs ++ ys).
children.closed_by: intros. in_crush. destruct x; simpl in *; eauto.

children.name: post_input_analyze_sent_packet
children.statement:
forall h p ms l,
  In p (map (fun m => mkPacket h (fst m) (snd m)) ms ++ l) ->
  (In (pDst p, pBody p) ms /\ h = pSrc p) \/ In p l.
children.closed_by: intros. in_crush; destruct x; simpl in *; eauto.

children.name: nw_nw_distinct_pairs_and_elim
children.statement:
forall xs a b ys l,
  l = xs ++ a :: ys ->
  In b (xs ++ ys) ->
  distinct_pairs_and network_network_invariant l ->
  network_network_invariant a b.
children.closed_by: induction xs; intros; subst; simpl in *; intuition eauto; subst; eauto. apply network_network_invariant_sym. eauto.

children.name: distinct_pairs_and_app_cons
children.statement:
forall A R xs p ys l,
  l = (xs ++ p :: ys) ->
  distinct_pairs_and (A:=A) R l ->
  distinct_pairs_and R (xs ++ ys).
children.closed_by: induction xs; intros; subst; simpl in *; intuition eauto.

children.name: distinct_pairs_and_app
children.statement:
forall A R l1 l2,
  distinct_pairs_and (A := A) R l1 ->
  distinct_pairs_and R l2 ->
  (forall x y, In x l1 -> In y l2 -> R x y) ->
  distinct_pairs_and R (l1 ++ l2).
children.closed_by: induction l1; intros; simpl in *; intuition. find_apply_lem_hyp in_app_or. intuition eauto.

applicability.goal_shape: A goal `inductive_invariant step_async step_async_init I` whose invariant `I` is a conjunction of a state invariant, a per-packet `network_invariant`, and a pairwise `distinct_pairs_and network_network_invariant` over the packet list; the step relation `step_async` is inductively defined with a small fixed set of constructors (here: input and deliver).
applicability.use_when: the step relation's constructors are the only branching and the effect of each constructor on each conjunct has already been packaged as a class field or a small list lemma, so `invcs` + `intuition` + `eauto using ...` closes every case.
applicability.avoid_when: the invariant is not a conjunction (so `intuition` cannot fan the goal into the conjuncts), or a single constructor's case needs a genuinely new argument not already a field or lemma; then the real content is a strengthened invariant or a key lemma, not the split itself.

claims.claim: The file is part of the project's CI build: `.github/workflows/docker-action.yml` runs docker-coq-action on `coq-verdi.opam`, whose `build:` is `make`, and `Makefile` turns `_CoqProject` into `coq_makefile`; `_CoqProject` lists `theories/Core/StatePacketPacketDecomposition.v` (line 17).
No `admit`, `Admitted`, `axiom` or `sorry` appears anywhere in the file, and the parent and all five children close with `Qed`.
claims.evidence: grep -nE 'admit|Admitted|axiom|Axiom|sorry' over the copied file theories/Core/StatePacketPacketDecomposition.v returned no matches; the Lemma/Theorem bodies at lines 117-207 each end in `Qed`.

claims.claim: The main proof is 34 lines (174-207) and, via `invcs H` on `step_async`, fans into 6 cases that call directly on 5 same-file lemmas; none of the 5 lemmas calls another, so the lemma depth below the theorem is 1.
claims.evidence: count over the copied file: proof body lines 174-207 = 34 lines; `invcs H` at line 179 opens the 6 `+` bullets at lines 180, 181, 188, 195, 196, 200; the 5 child lemmas are at 117-124, 126-133, 137-146, 148-155, 157-170, and each of their proofs ends without citing another of the five.

claims.claim: The author states why `nw_nw_distinct_pairs_and_elim` is specialised to `network_network_invariant` rather than generalised over the relation: 'NB: generalizing this over R makes it useless to [eauto using] because the conclusion is too general.'

metrics.how_counted: proof body = lines 174-207 of the copied file (statement at 172-173 not counted); case_count = the 6 `+` bullets opened by `invcs H` at line 179; children = the 5 same-file lemmas the proof cites; each child's proof is a single induction + `intuition`/`in_crush`/`eauto`, i.e. closed by automation with no intervening named lemma.

consequences: `invcs H` on `step_async` creates one goal per constructor and `intuition` further fans each into the three conjuncts of `composed_invariant`, so the case count is constructors x conjuncts (here 6). Exhaustiveness is the whole obligation: the split is sound only because `invcs` enumerates every constructor of `step_async`; adding a constructor to `step_async` later breaks the `Qed`. The glue carries no mathematics of its own — every `eauto using` names a `Decomposition` class field or one of the five list lemmas — so it breaks if a field's statement is reworded or a lemma is generalised (the author's comment at lines 135-136 warns of exactly this).
